clusters.title: `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` queue starvation: jobs cancelled without ever getting a runner — 6 cancelled, 7 queued

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
All 6 MI35x 1-GPU jobs in N28 waited 13 h 13 min with no runner. The run was then cancelled at 06:49 UTC by a maintainer. No test ran, so these jobs are not test failures.
Still queued at snapshot:
AO: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (rocm10, 0)` and `(rocm10, 1)`, since 13:12.
AP: `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x (rocm720)`, since 19:06.
N29a and N29b: `nightly-test-1-gpu-mi35x` and `nightly-1-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-flash-next-fp8`, 2 jobs each.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` infrastructure: demand on this pool exceeds its capacity.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: [#47162](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47162) (retimed the schedules) and [#47244](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47244) (merged the MI35x 1-GPU jobs) both landed before AO and AP, and the queue did not drain. That suggests too few runners online rather than too much load.
✅ [#47150](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47150) (open, `blocked`).
⚠️ [#46015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46015) (open, `dirty`).
Neither moves the nightly gpu-1 jobs off this pool.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: runner owners count the online `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` runners. Re-dispatch N28's qwen38 MI35x legs once capacity is back.

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`: before [#47244](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47244) ([`686cf984`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/686cf984704b79cb1b3f7145827c6f1922c4445d)), `call-pr-test-amd-extra` was `skipped` on every scheduled run. AP is its first scheduled run. All three clusters predate it.

details.label: R344
details.text: `[MEDIUM]`: torch.compile CUDA-graph capture is invalidated on rocm720.
Mechanism: a Triton `CompiledKernel.__del__` calls `hipModuleUnload` during capture (`Code: 900`), and `hipblasCreate` fails after that.
`test_torch_compile_moe.py` has failed 14 of 16 rocm720 runs since Oct 14, and failed back to at least Sep 26. It passes on rocm10 and rocm724. No change is blamed.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: intermittent (Oct 28 passed cleanly), and not reproduced.
Fix: ⚠️ [#35427](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35427) (`dirty`; its author says it does not fix this trigger).

details.label: R345
details.text: `[MEDIUM]`: a flaky perf threshold. The bs=10 `avg_latency_ms` was 60.60 against a 60 ms bound.
8 of 10 rocm720 values sit 0.2–1.75 ms under the bound. It also failed on Oct 23.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: both recent rocm720 runs failed, which fits a ~1 ms mean shift equally well.
Fix: ❌.

details.label: R346
details.text: `[MEDIUM]`: a long-standing Mooncake HIP-IPC offset defect. The destination `input_layernorm.weight` comes back zeroed whenever the test draws `transfer_engine`. The same failure happened on rocm10 on Sep 21.
Fix: ✅ [#46779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46779) (open, `blocked`). It needs AMD validation.
